title: Soil microbiome engineering for crops
bottleneck: The soil microbiome governs nutrient cycling, disease suppression, and stress tolerance, but it's a complex ecosystem of thousands of interacting species that resists simple engineering — inoculants that work in the lab routinely fail in the field because native microbes outcompete them. We can't yet predict which microbial consortia will establish, persist, and function in a given soil, making microbiome products unreliable. why_it_blocks: A working microbiome toolkit could replace much synthetic fertilizer and pesticide use; its unreliability keeps farmers dependent on chemical inputs.
current_state: Commercial inoculants like rhizobia and mycorrhizae work for specific pairings; general engineered microbiomes remain a research frontier.
